name: get_root_motion_track
description: get_root_motion_track({asset_path,bone?,start_frame=0,end_frame=last,max_keys=512})->asset_path,bone,number_of_keys,start_frame,end_frame,stride,keys[{frame,time,x,y,z,pitch,yaw,roll}]; results are decimated with `stride` when the range exceeds `max_keys`.

name: set_root_motion_keys
description: set_root_motion_keys({asset_path,bone?,keys:[{frame,x?,y?,z?,pitch?,yaw?,roll?}],save=false})->asset_path,bone,number_of_keys,applied_keys,dirty,saved?; per-key partial update, unlisted channels keep their current value, so Z can be moved on its own. Rejects a `frame` outside the sequence range.

name: flatten_root_motion_axis
description: flatten_root_motion_axis({asset_path,bone?,axis="z",value=0,start_frame=0,end_frame=last,blend_frames=0,save=false})->asset_path,bone,axis,value,touched_keys,dirty,saved?; drives one translation channel to `value` over the range, easing in across `blend_frames` so the flattened tail does not pop. Use for an animation that ends off the ground: `{axis:"z",value:0,blend_frames:N}`.

name: get_bone_component_transform
description: get_bone_component_transform({asset_path,bone?|bones:[names],start_frame=0,end_frame=last,max_keys=256})->asset_path,space="component",number_of_keys,start_frame,end_frame,stride,keys[{frame,time,bones{name:{x,y,z,pitch,yaw,roll}}}]; composes each bone up the reference-skeleton parent chain, so translations are relative to the mesh component origin rather than the parent bone. Bones without a track fall back to the ref pose. Use to compare two sequences in the same space - e.g. where a weapon hand is at the contact frame versus where the target's chest is.

name: list_skeleton_bones
description: list_skeleton_bones({asset_path,query?})->asset_path,skeleton,bone_count,returned,bones[{index,name,parent,has_track}]; `query` is a substring filter on the bone name.

name: inspect_anim_notifies
description: inspect_anim_notifies({asset_path,class_filter?,include_properties=true})->asset_path,asset_class,play_length,frame_rate?,tracks[{index,name}],sections?[{name,start_time}],notify_count,notifies[{index,kind,name,class,time,frame?,duration?,end_time?,track_index,track,trigger_chance,properties?{}}]; `kind` is `notify`, `state` or `named` (skeleton notify). `class_filter` matches the notify class name, the name without `_C`, or a path substring. `properties` lists the editable properties the notify class adds, as exported text. `index` is what `remove_anim_notify` takes.

name: add_anim_notify
description: add_anim_notify({asset_path,notify_class,time?,frame?,anchor?{class,edge="begin",offset=0},duration?,track?,create_track=true,properties?{},trigger_chance=1.0,skip_duplicates=true,save=false})->asset_path,added[notify],skipped[{time,reason}],notify_count,dirty,saved?; pass exactly one of `time`, `frame` or `anchor`. `notify_class` is a class path such as `/Script/Project_S.SoundFeedbackAnimNotify` or a Blueprint notify `/Game/.../ANS_X.ANS_X_C`. `anchor` places one notify per existing notify whose class matches `anchor.class`, at its `begin` or `end` edge plus `offset` seconds, clamped into the animation. A notify state needs `duration`. `track` defaults to the first track and is created when missing. `properties` values are property text; a gameplay tag property also takes a bare tag name and rejects an unregistered tag. `skip_duplicates` skips a placement that already has the same class, time and property values, so re-running a call is harmless. Example: `{asset_path:"/Game/.../AM_Torch_Attack01",notify_class:"/Script/Project_S.SoundFeedbackAnimNotify",anchor:{class:"ANS_Mob_AttackCollision",edge:"begin",offset:-0.05},properties:{soundTag:"Sound.Combat.Swing"}}`.

name: remove_anim_notify
description: remove_anim_notify({asset_path,index?,indices?:[int],class?,time?,confirm,save=false})->asset_path,removed[notify],notify_count,dirty,saved?; destructive and requires `confirm=true`. Pass one of `index`, `indices` (both from `inspect_anim_notifies`) or `class` (optionally narrowed to one `time`).

name: inspect_ik_retargeter
description: inspect_ik_retargeter({asset_path})->asset_path,source{ik_rig,preview_mesh,current_retarget_pose,retarget_poses[],bone_rotation_offsets[{bone,pitch,yaw,roll,angle}],bone_rotation_offset_count,root_translation_offset{x,y,z}},target{...},chain_mapping[{target_chain,source_chain,mapped}],chain_count. Reads a retargeter without changing it. Only bones whose stored delta exceeds 0.001 degrees are listed, so an unedited pose reports an empty array rather than the whole skeleton as identity.

name: create_retarget_pose
description: create_retarget_pose({asset_path,name,source_or_target="target",duplicate_from?,set_current=true,save=false})->asset_path,pose,source_or_target,current_retarget_pose,dirty,saved?. `duplicate_from` copies an existing pose instead of starting from the reference pose. Make a new pose before aligning rather than editing the one in use: it keeps the old result intact for an A/B and for a one-field rollback.

name: set_retarget_pose_bone_rotation
description: set_retarget_pose_bone_rotation({asset_path,bone,rotation{pitch,yaw,roll}|{x,y,z,w},source_or_target="target",mode="set"|"compose",save=false})->asset_path,bone,source_or_target,pose,mode,previous_offset,offset,dirty,saved?. Writes one bone's delta in the current retarget pose. `set` replaces the stored delta; `compose` post-multiplies onto it, which is what an iterative correction pass wants because each pass only measures the residual the previous one left.

name: auto_align_retarget_pose
description: auto_align_retarget_pose({asset_path,source_or_target="target",method="chain_to_chain",bones?[names],save=false})->asset_path,source_or_target,pose,requested_bone_count,bone_rotation_offset_count,largest_offset_degrees,largest_offset_bone,dirty,saved?. This is the editor's Auto-Align. Methods: `chain_to_chain` (uses the mapped retarget chains - the usual choice), `mesh_to_mesh` (skinned geometry direction, for leaf bones with no chain tangent), `local_rotation_axes`/`global_rotation_axes` (only correct when both skeletons share axis conventions). **Omitting `bones` resets the entire pose first**, so a full align discards manual corrections; pass `bones` to align a subset without touching the rest. Both preview meshes must be set on the retargeter or the call fails with `align_failed`, because alignment resolves the asset onto real skeletons.

name: reset_retarget_pose
description: reset_retarget_pose({asset_path,pose?,bones?[names],source_or_target="target",save=false})->asset_path,pose,source_or_target,reset_bone_count,dirty,saved?; empty `bones` resets every bone in the pose. `pose` defaults to the current one.

name: retarget_animations
description: retarget_animations({retargeter,animations:[paths],destination_path?,prefix?,suffix?,search?,replace?,source_mesh?,target_mesh?,include_referenced=false,overwrite=false,export_only_animated_bones=true})->retargeter,source_mesh,target_mesh,destination_path,requested,created[],created_count,overwrite,missing_animations?. Batch duplicate-and-retarget, the same operation as the editor's "Retarget Animation Assets" dialog. Meshes default to the retargeter's preview meshes. `include_referenced` is off by default here: a flat list of sequences would otherwise drag in the montages and blendspaces that reference them. `overwrite=true` replaces existing files in place instead of appending a numeric suffix - which is what re-exporting a set after fixing the retarget pose wants, and which **discards notifies, curves and sync markers authored on the previous results**.

name: create_level_sequence
description: create_level_sequence({package_path,display_rate=30,tracks:[{spawnable,animation?,start_frame=0}],save=false})->asset_path,package,display_rate,tick_resolution,playback_end_tick,tracks[{spawnable,binding_id,animation?,start_frame?,play_length?}],dirty,saved?. `/Game` only; rejects an existing package. `spawnable` takes a Blueprint asset path or a native class path and is added as a spawnable binding. `animation` adds a skeletal animation section on that binding; `start_frame` is in display frames and is converted to tick resolution for placement. Playback range is set to the longest track. Sequencer errors include `invalid_arguments,already_exists,load_failed,create_failed`.

name: inspect_level_sequence
description: inspect_level_sequence({asset_path,at_frame?,include_keys=false,max_keys=128})->asset_path,name,display_rate,tick_resolution,playback_start,playback_end,at_frame?,bindings[{binding_id,name,kind,class?,parent_binding_id?,template_class?,template_transform?,tracks[{type,sections[{type,start_frame?,end_frame?,animation?,animation_length?,slot_name?,constraint_binding_id?,attach_socket?,attach_component?,channels[{name,type,key_count,value?,stride?,keys?}],evaluated_transform?}]}],transform_at_frame?,transform_source?}],root_tracks[]. Reads a level sequence without changing it. Attach sections report the binding they follow and the socket (bone) and component they attach to; a component binding reports the binding it is parented to. Frames in and out are display frames, converted to tick resolution internally. `at_frame` evaluates every double and float channel at that frame and rebuilds a transform from a transform section, reporting it as `transform_at_frame` with `transform_source` of `transform_track`, `template` or `none`; only a section whose range contains the frame is evaluated. `template_transform` is the spawnable preview actor root relative transform, which is where a binding stands when no transform track drives it. `include_keys` dumps channel keys, decimated with `stride` past `max_keys`. Sequencer errors include `invalid_arguments,load_failed`.

name: set_level_sequence_channel_keys
description: set_level_sequence_channel_keys({asset_path,binding,channel,keys:[{frame,value}],save=false})->asset_path,binding,channel,track_type,updated_keys,added_keys,key_count,dirty,saved?. Writes float or double channel keys on one binding. `binding` is the binding name or id and `channel` the channel name, both as `inspect_level_sequence` reports them (e.g. `hand_r_CONTROL.Rotation.X` on a Control Rig track); the first matching channel on the binding is used. `frame` is a display frame. An existing key at that frame keeps its interpolation and only has its value replaced; a missing one is added. Auto tangents are rebuilt once after the writes, and the whole call is one undo step. `/Game` only. Sequencer errors include `invalid_arguments,load_failed,binding_not_found,channel_not_found,write_failed`.

name: open_level_sequence
description: open_level_sequence({asset_path})->asset_path,opened. Opens the sequence in Sequencer; a Control Rig section reports no channels until this has happened once in the editor session.

name: bake_level_sequence_animation
description: bake_level_sequence_animation({asset_path,binding,package_path,skeleton?,save=false})->asset_path,sequence,binding,play_length,number_of_keys,frame_rate,has_data_model,dirty,saved?. Bakes a skeletal mesh binding to a new AnimSequence through the engine's Sequencer export (transforms, morph targets, attribute and material curves, local space). Samples at the sequence display rate with no custom time range, matching the editor dialog defaults. Refuses a `package_path` that already exists, including an unpulled LFS pointer on disk, with `already_exists`. Errors also include `bake_failed,create_failed`. `skeleton` is required when the binding has no animation section, such as a Control Rig only binding. Open a Control Rig sequence with `open_level_sequence` first: without that, every other baked frame can come out in the reference pose. Check the result with `get_bone_component_transform`.

name: set_level_sequence_animation
description: set_level_sequence_animation({asset_path,binding,animation,create_section=false,save=false})->asset_path,animation,animation_length,previous_animations,section_count,dirty,saved?. Points every skeletal animation section on the binding at `animation`, leaving section ranges unchanged. `create_section` adds a section at the playback start when the binding has none. One undo step.

name: remove_level_sequence_track
description: remove_level_sequence_track({asset_path,binding,track_type,save=false})->asset_path,track_type,removed_count,purged_count,dirty,saved?. Removes every track of class `track_type` (as `inspect_level_sequence` reports it, e.g. `MovieSceneControlRigParameterTrack`) from the binding and moves it, plus any unlisted track of that class left in the package, out of the package so saves drop it. One undo step.

name: copy_level_sequence_bindings
description: copy_level_sequence_bindings({source_asset_path,target_asset_path,bindings:[],include_children=true,allow_unresolved=false,save=false})->source_asset_path,target_asset_path,copied[{binding_id,name,parent_binding_id?,custom_binding,reference_count,track_count,source_track_count}],unresolved[],dirty,saved?. Copies bindings (names or ids as `inspect_level_sequence` reports them) from one level sequence into another with their GUIDs, spawnable custom bindings and preview actor templates, locators and every track, so attach sections keep their socket and the binding they follow. `include_children` also copies component bindings parented to a selected binding. Everything is validated before the first write: refuses a GUID the target already has (`already_exists`), a parent the target lacks (`parent_missing`), a legacy spawnable (`unsupported`), a template name already in the target movie scene (`name_collision`), and an attach section following a binding the target lacks (`unresolved_reference`, listing them, unless `allow_unresolved`). Target `/Game` only; one undo step.

name: spawn_level_actor
description: spawn_level_actor({class,location?,yaw=0,label?})->object_path,label,location,dirty. Places an actor in the open editor level; the level stays dirty until saved. One undo step.

name: pie_control
description: pie_control({action,path?})->action,running,queued,world?,time_seconds?. `action` is start, stop, status, screenshot or save_level. `screenshot` writes the active viewport to the absolute `path` on the next rendered frame. `save_level` saves the open level on the next editor tick; use it for levels with landscape, because `save_asset` and `save_all_dirty` save inside the request and that asserts in the task graph when a landscape package is saved.

name: pie_call_actor_function
description: pie_call_actor_function({actor,command})->actor,called. Calls a function by name on a PIE actor found by name or label; `command` is the function name followed by its arguments.

name: pie_get_actor_state
description: pie_get_actor_state({actor?,bones?:[]})->actor,location,yaw,time_seconds,bones?,view_target?,camera_location?. Reads a PIE actor, or the player pawn when `actor` is omitted, with world space bone locations from its mesh.

name: inspect_niagara_system
description: inspect_niagara_system({asset_path,emitter?,query?,include_constants=true,limit=200})->asset_path,emitter_count,emitters[{index,name,enabled,local_space,determinism,renderers[],stateless?}],user_parameters[{name,type,value}],constants[{emitter,script,name,type,value}],constants_truncated. `query` is a substring filter applied to both parameter lists; `emitter` narrows to one emitter and accepts `System` for the system scripts. `renderers` names the renderer class per emitter, which is how you tell a ribbon core jet from a sprite splash.

name: set_niagara_user_parameter
description: set_niagara_user_parameter({asset_path,parameter,value,save=false})->asset_path,parameter,type,previous_value,value,saved?. `parameter` takes `Velocity` or `User.Velocity`. `value` accepts a number, `[x,y,z]`, `{x,y,z}`/`{r,g,b,a}`, or a vector spelled as a string (`X=0,Y=0,Z=1`, `0 0 1`, `[0,0,1]`) - MCP clients serialise an untyped value as a string, so the string form is what a multi-channel write usually arrives as. A bare number fills every channel, and a colour or quat may omit its last component. Writable types: float, int, bool, vec2/3/4, position, color, quat.

name: set_niagara_module_input
description: set_niagara_module_input({asset_path,emitter,parameter,value,compile=false,save=false})->asset_path,emitter,scripts[],parameter,type,previous_value,value,compiled?,saved?. `emitter` is an emitter name or `System`. `parameter` takes the full `Constants.<Emitter>.<Module>.<Input>` name or any trailing part of it, e.g. `AddVelocityInCone.Cone Axis`; a partial name matching more than one parameter name is rejected with the candidates rather than resolved arbitrarily. One name can live in several scripts - a module in both the particle spawn and particle update stacks keeps a copy in each, and interpolated spawn replays update logic - so every copy is written and `scripts` reports which ones. `value` follows the same rules as `set_niagara_user_parameter`.

name: add_niagara_emitter
description: add_niagara_emitter({asset_path,source_asset_path,new_name?,compile=true,save=false})->asset_path,source_asset_path,emitter,handle_id,emitter_count,compiled?,saved?; copies the emitter rather than referencing it, so retuning the copy cannot reach back into the source asset. The name is made unique against the existing handles, and `new_name` renames it afterwards. Compiles by default because an emitter that was never compiled does nothing when the system plays. **`source_asset_path` must name a standalone NiagaraEmitter asset**; a NiagaraSystem is refused with `unsupported_source`. An emitter embedded in a system cannot be copied out of it - the copy keeps its inheritance, so `VersionedParent` in its `VersionData` still points at a private subobject of the source package, and SavePackage then rejects every later save of the destination with "Illegal reference to private object". The add itself appears to succeed, which makes that a worse failure than refusing up front. Copying an emitter between two systems is a clipboard operation in the editor UI and is not reachable from here.

name: set_niagara_emitter_property
description: set_niagara_emitter_property({asset_path,emitter,enabled?,local_space?,compile=true,save=false})->asset_path,emitter,enabled,local_space,applied[],compiled?,saved?; at least one of `enabled`/`local_space` is required. `local_space=false` is what keeps droplets and decals behind in world space when the emitting actor moves.

name: compile_niagara_system
description: compile_niagara_system({asset_path,force=false,save=false})->asset_path,compiled,force,saved?; requests a compile and waits for it, so a save that follows writes compiled scripts rather than stale ones.

name: find_blueprint_assets
description: find_blueprint_assets({path|content_path="/Game",query,parent_class|exact_parent_class,derived_from|derives_from|base_class,blueprint_asset_class|asset_class,recursive=true,load_assets=true,include_only_on_disk_assets=false,exclude_paths=[],limit=200})->blueprints[asset identity, blueprint_asset_class,parent_class,generated_class,skeleton_generated_class,asset-registry class tags,display/category,is_data_only,loaded,status,match flags,type_filter_mode],counts. `load_assets=true` verifies inheritance exactly; false uses AssetRegistry tags.

name: inspect_blueprint_git_revision
description: inspect_blueprint_git_revision({asset_path,revision,...inspect_opts})->inspect_blueprint shape + source_asset_path,revision,repo_root,relative_filename,temp_asset_filename; working tree unchanged; Git filters/LFS applied.

name: find_functions
description: find_functions({query,class_path,limit=50})->functions[{name,owner_class,blueprint_callable,blueprint_pure,static,parameters[{name,type,direction,default?}]}]; provide at least query or class_path.

name: add_widget
description: add_widget({asset_path,widget_class,name,parent?,index=-1,width?,height?,texture?,text?,font_size?})->asset_path,name,widget_class,object_path,parent; Widget Blueprint only. Omit `parent` to set the root; `index` inserts at that child position instead of appending. Size, texture, and text options apply to compatible widget classes.

name: remove_widget
description: remove_widget({asset_path,name,confirm,allow_referenced=false})->removed[],dangling_references[]; deletes the widget and its children like the designer does; refuses while graph nodes use any of them unless allow_referenced.

name: move_widget
description: move_widget({asset_path,name,parent,dest_asset_path?,index=-1,allow_referenced=false})->object_path,index,moved?,dangling_references?; reparents or reorders inside one Widget Blueprint, or with `dest_asset_path` moves the widget and its children into another one, keeping designer properties and slot layout. Across assets it refuses while source graph nodes use the widgets unless allow_referenced; copy those nodes with `copy_nodes` first.

name: copy_nodes
description: copy_nodes({asset_path,graph,nodes:[id|name],dest_asset_path?,dest_graph?,offset_x=0,offset_y=0})->nodes[{source_id,id,object_name,class,title,x,y}],skipped[],missing_self_functions[]; editor copy-paste between graphs or Blueprints. Links among copied nodes are kept, links to other nodes are dropped. Entry/result nodes are skipped. Self members resolve by name in the destination, so add its variables and functions before compiling.

name: add_blueprint_interface
description: add_blueprint_interface({asset_path,interface_class})->asset_path,interface_class,added,already_implemented; adds a native or Blueprint interface to an existing Blueprint and leaves it dirty until saved.

name: delete_variable
description: delete_variable({asset_path,variable|name,confirm,allow_referenced=false,reference_path="/Game"})->deleted variable metadata; rejects without confirm; blocks referenced unless allowed.

name: retarget_function_call
description: retarget_function_call({asset_path,graph,node,target_class,target_function})->old_node,new_node,target_function; preserves same-name pin links/defaults if target signature allows.

name: set_property
description: set_property({asset_path?,target="class_default"|component,component?,object_path?,property,value})->property; supported value families: bool,int,float/double,string/name/text,enum,object/class/soft refs,vector,rotator,transform,color,array(simple); any other struct or array also accepts its Unreal text form as a string, e.g. ((BranchFilters=((BoneName=spine_01,BlendDepth=1)))).

name: diff_asset_against_git_revision
description: diff_asset_against_git_revision({asset_path,revision})->repo_root,relative_filename,temp_asset_filename; opens Unreal native diff, no checkout, exports `.uasset/.umap` sidecars `.uexp/.ubulk/.uptnl`, Git filters/LFS applied.

name: create_datatable
description: create_datatable({asset_path,row_struct,save=false})->asset_path,row_struct_path,saved?; empty table, `row_struct` is `/Script/Module.StructName` or a bare struct name, must derive from FTableRowBase; `/Game` only, rejects an existing asset.

name: set_datatable_row
description: set_datatable_row({asset_path,row_name,values{column:value},create_if_missing=false,save=false})->row_name,created,applied_columns,values,saved?; partial update, unlisted columns keep current values.

name: set_material_property
description: set_material_property({asset_path,property|property_path,value,recompile=true,save=false})->material summary; supports editable `UMaterial` properties such as `BlendMode`, `TwoSided`, `DitherOpacityMask`, `OpacityMaskClipValue`.

name: create_material_expression
description: create_material_expression({asset_path,class_path,x=0,y=0,selected_asset?,properties?})->expression; `class_path` accepts full class paths such as `/Script/Engine.MaterialExpressionSphereMask` or short names such as `SphereMask`.

name: set_material_expression_property
description: set_material_expression_property({asset_path,expression,property|property_path,value})->expression; `expression` accepts expression id, object name, or path.

name: setup_camera_cutout_material
description: setup_camera_cutout_material({asset_path,replace_existing=true,confirm=false,save=false,player_location_parameter="PlayerLocation",radius_parameter="CutoutRadius",hardness_parameter="CutoutHardness",radius=220,hardness=35}); configures a masked/dithered material with `WorldPosition -> SphereMask(A)`, `PlayerLocation -> SphereMask(B)`, radius/hardness scalar parameters, `OneMinus -> OpacityMask`, and a neutral base color.

name: inspect_gameplay_ability
description: inspect_gameplay_ability({asset_path})->parent/generated class,policy fields,major tag containers,cooldown/cost GE refs,ability-task-like nodes.

name: set_gameplay_tag_container
description: set_gameplay_tag_container({asset_path,known_field|property_path,tags:[...]}); known fields:`AbilityTags,ActivationOwnedTags,ActivationRequiredTags,ActivationBlockedTags,CancelAbilitiesWithTag,BlockAbilitiesWithTag,SourceRequiredTags,SourceBlockedTags,TargetRequiredTags,TargetBlockedTags,GrantedTags,AssetTags,ApplicationTagRequirements,OngoingTagRequirements,RemoveEffectsWithTags`. GE `GrantedTags` target-actor tags via `UTargetTagsGameplayEffectComponent`; `AssetTags` asset tags via `UAssetTagsGameplayEffectComponent`.

name: configure_ability_cooldown
description: configure_ability_cooldown|configure_ability_cost({asset_path,effect}) set exposed cooldown/cost class defaults when present.

name: configure_ability_cost
description: configure_ability_cooldown|configure_ability_cost({asset_path,effect}) set exposed cooldown/cost class defaults when present.

name: inspect_attribute_references
description: inspect_attribute_references({path="/Game",attribute?,exclude_paths=[],limit?}); `generate_attribute_set_cpp(...)` guarded unsupported unless future generator enabled.

name: generate_attribute_set_cpp
description: generate_attribute_set_cpp({...}) - guarded, reports unsupported unless a future generator is enabled.

name: list_statetree_related_blueprints
description: list_statetree_related_blueprints({path="/Game",query,exclude_paths=[],limit=500})->blueprints likely task/condition/evaluator/utility by parent class and STT/STC/STE naming.

selected_actor.description: select the currently selected editor actor
select the currently selected editor actor
select the currently selected editor actor
select the currently selected editor actor
select the currently selected editor actor
select the currently selected editor actor

name: statetree_compare_runtime_to_asset
description: statetree_compare_runtime_to_asset({asset_path,selector})->runtime state mapped into static hierarchy plus outgoing analysis.

selected_actor.description: select the currently selected editor actor
select the currently selected editor actor

name: spawn_node
description: spawn_node({asset_path,graph,node_type,x=0,y=0,function?,class_path?,variable?,event_name?,call_in_editor?})->node; node_type:`branch|call_function|variable_get|variable_set|custom_event`. Prefer `spawn_blueprint_action` for action DB nodes and `spawn_native_event` for engine events.

name: format_blueprint_graph
description: DEPRECATED: automatic node placements are unreadable for humans. Prefer manually chosen NodePosX/NodePosY with set_property. Both control_flow_parameters and dependency_layered require allow_deprecated_automatic_layout=true for legacy execution.

name: add_anim_state
description: add_anim_state({asset_path,graph,name,x=0,y=0,always_reset_on_entry?})->asset_path,state_machine_graph,state_name,node,state_graph,always_reset_on_entry; `graph` is a state machine graph name or its `path` from inspect_blueprint. Fill the new state's pose with spawn_blueprint_action on `state_graph`.

name: add_anim_transition
description: add_anim_transition({asset_path,graph,from_state,to_state,crossfade_duration?,priority_order?})->asset_path,state_machine_graph,from_state,to_state,node,crossfade_duration,priority_order,rule_graph,result_node,result_pin; states by name, node id or object name. Wire a bool into `result_node`.`result_pin` (bCanEnterTransition) on `rule_graph` with spawn_node/connect_pins. Graph arguments accept a graph name or its `path` (inspect_blueprint `graphs[].path`) when names repeat.
